### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/translation.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via translatePage (symbol, a top-level function))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/translation.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **139** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json faf6348508519197c6047b46fb30b6ae8910f6b2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c572bb798073004731b40ea36ee88e3b9ef487f6` — the merge of head `194157f5e16b955ece5f95ad2a518d1d5679139e` into base `faf6348508519197c6047b46fb30b6ae8910f6b2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c572bb798073004731b40ea36ee88e3b9ef487f6 && git checkout c572bb798073004731b40ea36ee88e3b9ef487f6
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin faf6348508519197c6047b46fb30b6ae8910f6b2 194157f5e16b955ece5f95ad2a518d1d5679139e && git checkout -B drift-repro faf6348508519197c6047b46fb30b6ae8910f6b2 && git merge --no-ff 194157f5e16b955ece5f95ad2a518d1d5679139e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json faf6348508519197c6047b46fb30b6ae8910f6b2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs faf6348508519197c6047b46fb30b6ae8910f6b2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `194157f5e16b955ece5f95ad2a518d1d5679139e`
Local-runs: none

Read-only, all read at 2026-10-09T21:01Z: card #22508's body and every comment (triage `6085431021`, claim `6086910462`, dev report `6088963381`, seat answers `6089063944`), card #22536, PR #22534's body and file list, the net diff from merge-base `9411faa1ba` to the head, `i18n-extract.ts` (`sameAuthored` and its page-header call) and `PageHeaderProps.title` on `main`, and the head's check-runs. Nothing built, run or re-run; the derived gate families are answered by the check-runs below.

### ① Derived judgments

**Accept set: unchanged. Right.** `translation.zod.ts` changes the `pages.NAME.title` describe string and the `pages` JSDoc only; the field stays `z.string().optional()`; no key is added, retired or re-typed; no accepted value or default moves. `PageHeaderProps.title` (`component.zod.ts`, `I18nLabelSchema.optional()`) is untouched. A grep of `main` for the old phrases ("defaults to `label`", "title falls back to label", "falls back to `pages.NAME.label`") hits only the five files this diff rewrites, so no declaration of the old contract survives outside the PR. The extractor's own comments (a title that merely restates the page label resolves through the label's key) stay true under the new rule.

**Public surface: unchanged. Right.** `i18n-resolver.ts` adds three module-private functions (`authoredLabelText`, `sameAuthoredText`, `resolvePageHeaderTitle`); none is exported and `translatePage`'s signature is unchanged. `Type Check · source gates` and `Spec property liveness` are green on the head.

**Served behaviour at `GET /api/v1/meta/page/:name` and `GET /api/v1/meta/page`: narrowed to the ruled order. Right.** Read at the head: `translatePage` computes `bundleHeaderTitle` and `bundleLabel` page-wide, each through `lookupPageAttr` (walks the locale chain, skips empty strings; unchanged), and the one visitor passed to `walkAddressedPageComponents` calls `resolvePageHeaderTitle(bundleHeaderTitle, bundleLabel, next.properties?.title, doc.label)` for every `page:header` that arrives with `nested: false`. Both roots arrive that way: a region's `components[]` entries and every `slots.SLOT` entry are each visited through `visitComponent(c, 0)` and `nested` is "depth above zero". The spread then writes `title` only when the resolver answers one, so an `undefined` answer leaves the authored title alone even while the bundle subtitle is applied beside it. The order is: bundle `title`; else the authored title as written; else the bundle `label` only where `authoredLabelText(title)` is `undefined` or `sameAuthoredText(title, doc.label)` holds. That implements triage `6085431021`'s direction and its three pins, each pinned in `i18n-resolver.test.ts` at a region root and a slot root alike:
- a pack with `label` and no `title` keeps the authored `'{name}'`, in `en` and `zh-CN` (the measured hotcrm shape), for a plain string and for an inline locale map, and once more through `translateMetadataDocument('page', ...)`, the function the REST doors call;
- a pack with `title` replaces it;
- a header with no authored title (`{}`, `{ title: '' }`, subtitle only) still receives the bundle `label`.
Every label fill the new rule performs is one the old rule also performed, so nothing that rendered correctly before renders differently now; only the trap case changes.

**The refinement (label also stands in where the header title restates the page's own `label`): right, and the seat's answer A in `6089063944` is sound.** The triage's literal sentence rested on "expected: none" relying on the label over an authored title. The dev measured that reliance: the extractor's page-header pass deliberately offers no `pages.NAME.title` when `sameAuthored(props.title, page.label)`, three shipped Setup pages (`marketplace_installed`, `cloud_connection_settings`, `connect_agent`) are that shape with label-only packs in zh-CN, ja-JP and es-ES, and ablation leg 2 turned `platform-page-i18n-parity.test.ts` red. The refinement keeps the triage's own principle: when the authored title IS the label's text, the label's translation translates that very text and no attribute is swapped over different text. It is a strict subset of the old fill, resolver-only, and keeps the extractor/resolver pair on one rule; option B would widen the surface to two more packages and leave every externally extracted pack's header untranslated with no diagnostic. The PR names the reliance, as the triage asked.

**`sameAuthoredText` as a mirror of the extractor's `sameAuthored`: right on the cases the mirror decides, with two non-blocking observations.**
- String vs string: both compare the non-empty text (`a === other`; the extractor's `inlineText` equality). Same.
- Inline map vs map: both drop empty-string entries, treat an emptied map as no text, and compare sorted keys with entry-equal values, key order ignored. Same. A string against a map answers false in both.
- Both absent: the resolver reads the label (absent-title arm); the extractor's `sameAuthored(undefined, undefined)` is true, so it offers no `title` key. Same outcome.
- Empty-string title `''`: the resolver never consults the mirror; `authoredLabelText('')` is `undefined`, so the absent-title arm fills the label (pin 3, pinned by `{ title: '' }`). The extractor's `sameAuthored('', label)` is false and `pushEntry` accepts any string, so it offers a `pages.NAME.title` row with an empty seed. A predicate-level difference, not an outcome one: an empty bundle `title` is skipped by `lookupPageAttr`, a filled one wins by step 1, an omitted one gets the label; the header is neither left untranslated nor translated over different authored text. Pre-existing extractor behaviour outside this card's file surface. Observation only.
- The extractor's `inlineLocaleMap` also parses the map through `InlineLocaleMapSchema` (BCP-47 keys); the resolver's `authoredLabelText` does not. A map that fails that parse cannot reach `translatePage` through a validated document, since `PageHeaderProps.title` and the page `label` are both `I18nLabel`. Observation only.

**Docs and ledger: right.** `content/docs/references/system/translation.mdx` is the generated consequence of the describe edit (all three tables regenerated, text identical to the describe); `content/docs/ui/translations.mdx` restates the order and names both roots; the `translatePage` docblock restates it; `liveness/translation.json`'s `pages` row changes `evidence` and `note` text only, with status and verifiedAt untouched, and `Spec property liveness` is green.

**Test fixture `regionHeaderWithId` gains `label: 'Sales Home'`: right.** `PageSchema` requires `label`, and that fixture's header restates it, which is the shape whose title the page-name route answers from the label.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/22508-page-header-title-keeps-authored.md` declares `'@objectstack/spec': patch` and carries `Clause-②: no`; the PR body's second line is `Clause-②: no`. Both match the diff: no schema, key, accepted value, default or export changes; no arm is claimed and none applies, since nothing an author can write is newly accepted or newly rejected. What changes is served behaviour, a class (c) trap fixed at the default, which is a bug fix in a released package: patch is right, and `skip-changeset` would have been wrong. The changeset names what changes for an author (a header whose title differs from the label, in a locale whose pack carries `label` but no `title`, now shows the authored title; add `pages.NAME.title` to translate it), and the in-repo population of that shape is zero. `Check Changeset` is green on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flag: deviation from the triage's literal sentence** (`deviations[0]`, `open_questions[0]`). Answered: the seat ruled A in `6089063944`; judged sound in ①. The triage seat's objection window noted there is its own; nothing is owed by this record.
- **Dev flag: open question 2, an absent title on a record page.** Answered by escalation: the seat filed #22536 (`finding`, class (c), producer objectui `buildDefaultHeader`); its body names the ruled control, carries the dev's A/B/C and orders the work after this PR lands. Leaving the ruled control as is in this PR is correct: triage ruled that pin on this card, this diff does not change that behaviour (the old rule filled an absent title too), and overturning a triage pin is triage's call, not a dev's and not this review's.
- **Dev flag: file surface** (`deviations[1]`). The generated reference page and the liveness row are the declared-contract text the surface names, and `translation.zod.ts` is where the describe lives. Accepted; no other package is edited.
- **Dev flag: fixture edit** (`deviations[2]`). Judged right in ①.
- **Dev flag: container hygiene** (`deviations[3]`, two stray files at the container root). Outside the diff and outside any repo; nothing to escalate.
- **Out-of-scope finding: `check:platform-checklist` red on `main`.** Verified pre-existing and outside this diff: `ce3d0ad419` (PR #22513) removed the `canEdit(...)` member from `service-storage/src/attachment-access-hooks.ts`, the declaration the `attachments-storage` checklist item anchors; this diff touches neither that file nor `docs/qa/platform-checklist/**`. The gate is kept out of per-PR CI by maintainer decision (the note in `lint.yml`, `checklist-status.yml`), its standing caller is `platform-checklist-watchdog.yml` on `main`, and zero of the head's 32 check-runs is a checklist run. The seat's reading that the watchdog owns it stands; no card is owed by this PR.
- **Locale chain, unchanged** (PR acceptance note). A fallback-chain pack's `title` still beats the authored title. That is the bundle's own title, which the triage put first; not a flag.
- **Governed surfaces.** The file list touches none (`docs/adr/**`, `docs/NORTH-STAR.md`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`); head repo equals base repo, so this is not a fork PR. `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is green.
- **Check-runs on the head, read once at 2026-10-09T21:01Z and not awaited:** 32 total; 20 completed, of which 18 `success` and 2 `skipped` (`Console Pin Gate`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`); 12 `in_progress` (`Test Core` 1/6 to 6/6, `Dogfood Regression Gate` 2/3 and 3/3, `Temporal Conformance`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Type Check · workspace`); 0 failed. The in-progress runs are not judged green here. Completed green: Build Core, Build Docs, Dogfood Verify CLI, Dogfood Regression Gate 1/3, Type Check source, debt-ledger and consumer gates, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, the claim and single-writer checks, Check Documentation Links, Auto Label and the flag-docs check. Landing waits on the remainder converging, which is the owning seat's read, not this record's.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-22508-page-header-title-fallback`
Reviewed-by: `session_01VZqqwTj2wsihZEbfT6yyYN`

**VERDICT: PASS**

> `↳ 失败原因` 是判读的关键：**超时**（`Test timed out in …` / `Hook timed out in …`）多半是负载/时序，不是本 PR 的回归；
> **断言**（`AssertionError: …`）才指向真实的行为改变。两者的 `FAIL` 行长得一模一样，只有这一行能区分。
>
> ⚠️ **断言这一侧有一类例外，判据是断言在测什么，不是它是不是 `AssertionError`。** 断言的对象是**产品行为**（一个值、一个形状、一次拒收）⇒ 照上面读：真实的行为改变，去查，⛔ 不要重排掉；
> 断言的对象是**这次实验自身的有效性前提**（跑完的耗时、负载下的先后、任何只在时间预算内才成立的条件）⇒ 它跟**超时**是同一类，同样对负载敏感，重排一次是合法的判别手段。
> 识别是机械的：断言的消息或它比较的值本身点名了一段**时长、一个时间戳、一个耗时计数**。实测过的一对 —— `AssertionError: SecurityPlugin.init() ran: expected false to be true` 测的是产品行为（真回归）；
> `AssertionError: this run took over a second, so second-precision stamps could have differed too: expected 1006 to be less than 1000` 测的是实验前提：它守护的那条不变式当时是绿的，同一个 head 原样重排一次即成功。
> 穿着 `AssertionError` 外衣的时间测量，仍然是时间测量。（⛔ 这只改「怎么读一次红」，不改「哪些测试可以重排」——后者由别处管。）
